static_traits.name: Chen Kai
static_traits.social_status: Has a supportive group of friends, but Self-doubt and constant comparison affect friendships; has not yet discussed the specific 'not good enough' feelings with friends
static_traits.medical_history: No history of similar psychological problems; has not received psychotherapy; no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Can express clearly and do Reflection; Low mood, skeptical but willing to try; fairly cooperative with the counselor

basic_info.main_problem: I feel I cannot excel at hiking because I am not a world-class hiker, which causes Self-doubt and feelings of not being good enough.
basic_info.core_demands: Persistent self-doubt and 'not good enough' feelings are starting to affect my motivation for other hobbies and activities, prompting me to seek counseling.
growth_experiences: Started hiking as a hobby a few years ago and found it fun at first, but seeing others share better hiking performances and adventure experiences on social media, kept comparing and gradually worsened Self-doubt; although tried setting personal goals to improve hiking skill, struggled to maintain self-affirmation even after reaching goals, and this 'not good enough' feeling spread to other interests and activities, affecting friendships.

core_beliefs: Only being the best has worth / is enjoyable

special_situations.event: On social media, sees others share more outstanding hiking performances or adventures
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not world-class or the best, it equals not good enough and meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proves oneself by setting higher personal goals and extra practice
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They are all better than me; I am not good enough.

special_situations.event: When interacting with friends, notices the other person performs better in areas such as hiking
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am not as good as my friends, I will seem like a failure and not deserve to participate
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Social withdrawal, reducing contact with friends to avoid comparison
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not as good as them; being with them makes me seem even less good enough.

special_situations.event: Still feeling inadequate after reaching personally set hiking goals
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only reaching world-class level deserves affirmation; other progress does not count
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Raising standards, negating the value of progress already made
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This progress is not worth mentioning; still far from enough.

special_situations.event: When thinking about going hiking or planning a new hobby
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot become the best, it equals wasting time and being meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces motivation to try new activities, postpones or gives up
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Since I cannot be the best, there is no need to do it.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and seen as valuable and excellent
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being evaluated as not good enough, fear of failure and shame
defense_goal: Maintaining self-esteem by insisting on the 'must be the best' standard, avoiding exposing the not-good-enough self

object_relations.self_representation: A not-good-enough comparer, a self easily surpassed by others

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When counseling focuses on challenging the belief 'must become the best' or discussing setting non-comparative, enjoyment-oriented goals
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: The client may understand the counselor's inquiry as negating or weakening their standards (transference: Projecting the external sense of judgment into the counseling situation)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Use an empathic and non-judgmental tone; first validate the importance of 'standards' to them, then use open-ended questions to Guidance concretizing experiences and cost-benefit; avoid direct confrontation, inviting examples of pleasant moments when not at their best.

manifestations: Tightly binding the activity's meaning to whether it is 'world-class / the best', believing that 'if not the best it is a waste of time'
Enjoyment swallowed up by performance and comparison, doubting the inherent value of hiking
outcomes: Decreased drive, reduced participation in new hobbies and activities

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently using the inner rule of 'must / should be the best' to judge oneself
Binding enjoyment to world-class performance, negating positive experiences in non-top states

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Repeated self-comparison and Self-denial, worrying about 'not being good enough' and reducing participation in new activities
Withdrawal in friendships due to Self-doubt, cautiously expressing true feelings

positive_force: Has a supportive group of friends, able to provide emotional support
Can experience the joy of nature and some pleasure in the hiking activity itself
Willing to try new goal setting and cognitive restructuring (open attitude toward counseling)
negative_force: Black-and-white thinking and excessive comparison dominate meaning evaluation
Negating positive progress, struggling to internalize self-affirmation
Ties worth to external performance / world-class standards; overly relies on external comparison

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Self-doubt when thinking of hiking or seeing others' hiking shares, markedly lowering participation motivation
antecedent: Sees others sharing hiking adventures or better performances on social media
target_behavior.core_reason: The inner belief is 'only by becoming the very best is there meaning', driven by black-and-white thinking and comparison
target_behavior.function: Avoids failure and shame, relieving the threat of being judged in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Reduced enjoyment of hiking, overall Decreased drive, further affecting other interests and activities

target_behavior.behavior: Withdrawal in interactions with friends, reducing contact
antecedent: When interacting with friends, notices friends performing better
Thinking about possibly being compared or seen as 'not good enough'
target_behavior.core_reason: Self-worth overly dependent on external comparison and judgment, fearing exposure of not being good enough
target_behavior.function: Avoids feeling ashamed and judged, maintaining fragile self-esteem
target_behavior.consequence: Friendships are affected, reducing supportive interactions and positive experiences
